analysis:
Examined all supplied metadata, patches and source excerpts. This batch changes documentation only; it does not independently establish a runtime vulnerability. Selected-model recovery adds periodic load attempts and pre-load eviction, with documented selection/pin/lease protection, idle/dwell limits, backoff and ordinary memory admission (docs/architecture/hardware-support.md, added head lines 371–408). Add-on documentation extends hold refusal and cancellation to recovery and coordinator preloads (docs/architecture/addon-hold.md:67–70 head), consistent with A-018, TB-012 and T-059. No changed encryption, cache scope/TTL, key custody, attestation, authorization or billing control is evidenced; T-041's cache risks are not newly established by residency changes. Existing surrounding failure modes are not PR regressions.
Integration must verify ProviderLoop+SelectedModelRecovery.swift against load admission, eviction exclusions, request admission and enterAddonHold: cancellation must prevent slot publication and retain native ownership until retirement completes. Reconcile the idle-only victim description with the new policy that closes admission to an adopted, actively serving model after ten minutes (changelog.d/selected-models-recover.md:8 head); verify in-flight work drains, cold requests cannot immediately reload it, and protected models remain protected. Also examine the 15-second shutdown unload bound (same file:7) against native wired-residency ownership: hardware-support.md:219–225 base explicitly says timeout/cancellation is not restoration proof. Ensure the bound leads to process exit rather than live-process memory reuse or premature clean-retirement claims. These implementation contracts remain unverified because runtime source is outside this batch, not because a missing control has been observed.
